No steel L-track pier, cobalt coupe, or readable alley mouth appears in any supplied capture, unlike the labeled AI target.

fixes.evidence: The trace reports frame_count 4, samples 137 over duration 16.02 s, player_displacement 19.032 (XZ), stationary_grounded true, but performance_claim is 'unqualified; shared renderer and capture overhead' and capture_scope disclaims HUD/audio; no fence appears in frame-000/002/003 and no audio or collision-stop event is recorded.
fixes.issue: Acceptance items for >=60fps walking, collision stop at a fence, and footstep audio remain unevidenced by the supplied trace.

critic.summary: The native build runs and the controller walk trace is real (build_exit 0, player_exit 0, ~19.03 m horizontal displacement over ~16 s across 137 samples, stationary_grounded true, 0.158 m vertical drop), so movement and grounding are plausible. However, the three actual Unity captures do not support the task bar. Versus the labeled AI target, the native frames show a placeholder graybox scene: no HUD or minimap at all (acceptance explicitly requires a visible five-slot HUD), no steel L-track pier, no parked cobalt coupe, and no readable alley mouth or brick two-flat/greystone dressing — the block is an unlit facade row floating in a large empty brown plane, and two of three frames show the character in an empty void. Performance (>=60fps), fence collision and footstep audio are also unestablished (capture_scope and performance_claim explicitly disclaim them). Visible failures in supplied captures justify FIX rather than UNVERIFIED. Biggest observable gap: the captured native frames contain no HUD and omit the required L-track pier and cobalt coupe, presenting a graybox void instead of the specified Chicago street.
